bugs.name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Cavitating upper-lobe lung infection in heavy drinking
bugs.micro: Large gram-negative enteric bacillus; non-motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey); indole-negative, urease-positive, VP and citrate positive; huge polysaccharide capsule gives wet mucoid colonies that string out on a loop
bugs.presentation: 58-year-old man who drinks a pint of vodka daily, found asleep in a chair: 3 days of T 39.1 C and coughing thick, sticky, blood-streaked sputum. Film: dense right upper-lobe consolidation, the fissure sagging downward, with a 3-cm cavity; sputum: plump gram-negative rods.

bugs.name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Carbapenem-resistant bloodstream infection in the ICU
bugs.micro: Large gram-negative enteric bacillus; non-motile; ferments lactose (pink on MacConkey); indole-negative, urease-positive, VP and citrate positive; huge polysaccharide capsule gives wet mucoid colonies that string out on a loop
bugs.presentation: 72-year-old woman transferred from another hospital's ICU, 3 weeks of meropenem and a central line: T 39.3 C, BP 78/44, lactate 4.2 mmol/L. Blood cultures grow a lactose-fermenting gram-negative rod resistant to every beta-lactam; only colistin is active.

bugs.name: Bordetella pertussis
bugs.disease: Paroxysmal cough illness in an unimmunized infant
bugs.micro: Small gram-negative aerobic coccobacillus; fastidious, grown on a charcoal or high-blood selective medium; PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab; fimbriae and filamentous hemagglutinin anchor it to ciliated cells; three toxins, one raising cAMP
bugs.presentation: 6-week-old unimmunized infant, afebrile: 10 days of a runny nose, then bursts of 12-15 coughs with no breath between, ending in gagging, vomiting and blue lips, with 20-second pauses in breathing. Well between bursts, lungs clear; WBC 34,000/uL with 78% lymphocytes.

bugs.name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Slow-onset lung infection in a young adult with hemolysis
bugs.micro: Smallest free-living bacterium; no cell wall, so invisible on Gram stain and untouched by beta-lactams; sterols stabilize its membrane; grows slowly on Eaton agar; PCR; IgM clumps red cells at 4 C but not 37 C
bugs.presentation: 19-year-old military recruit in a barracks where several others are ill: 10 days of gradually worsening headache, malaise, low-grade fever and a nagging dry cough; he looks well and has only scattered crackles. Film: patchy bilateral opacities. Hb 10.2 g/dL, reticulocytes 6%.

bugs.name: Chlamydophila pneumoniae
bugs.disease: Slow-onset lung infection spread person to person by aerosol
bugs.micro: Obligate intracellular energy parasite that cannot make enough ATP; wall has little peptidoglycan (muramic acid reduced); inert infectious elementary body alternates with replicating reticulate body; Giemsa inclusions, PCR, serology
bugs.presentation: 48-year-old man whose wife had the same illness 3 weeks ago: 2 weeks of hoarseness, sore throat and a dry hacking cough, with T 37.9 C and no chills. Lungs nearly clear; film: patchy bilateral opacities. Na 139 mEq/L, no diarrhea; Hb 14 g/dL; sputum Gram stain shows no organisms.
